verses.text: Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and called for the elders of Israel, for their heads, for their judges, and for their officers; and they presented themselves before God.

Joshua said to all the people, “Yahweh says, the God of Israel, ‘Your fathers lived of old time beyond the River, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nahor: and they served other gods.
I took your father Abraham from beyond the River, and led him throughout all the land of Canaan, and multiplied his offspring,  and gave him Isaac.
I gave to Isaac Jacob and Esau: and I gave to Esau Mount Seir, to possess it. Jacob and his children went down into Egypt.
“‘I sent Moses and Aaron, and I plagued Egypt, according to that which I did among them: and afterward I brought you out.
I brought your fathers out of Egypt: and you came to the sea. The Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and with horsemen to the Red Sea.

When they cried out to Yahweh, he put darkness between you and the Egyptians, and brought the sea on them, and covered them; and your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. You lived in the wilderness many days.
“‘I brought you into the land of the Amorites, that lived beyond the Jordan. They fought with you, and I gave them into your hand. You possessed their land, and I destroyed them from before you.
Then Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel. He sent and called Balaam the son of Beor to curse you,
but I would not listen to Balaam; therefore he blessed you still. So I delivered you out of his hand.

“‘You went over the Jordan, and came to Jericho. The men of Jericho fought against you, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite; and I delivered them into your hand.
I sent the hornet before you, which drove them out from before you, even the two kings of the Amorites; not with your sword, nor with your bow.
I gave you a land whereon you had not labored, and cities which you didn’t build, and you live in them. You eat of vineyards and olive groves which you didn’t plant.’
“Now therefore fear Yahweh, and serve him in sincerity and in truth. Put away the gods which your fathers served beyond the River, in Egypt; and serve Yahweh.

If it seems evil to you to serve Yahweh, choose today whom you will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell; but as for me and my house, we will serve Yahweh.”
The people answered, “Far be it from us that we should forsake Yahweh, to serve other gods;

for it is Yahweh our God who brought us and our fathers up out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage, and who did those great signs in our sight, and preserved us in all the way in which we went, and among all the peoples through the middle of whom we passed.
Yahweh drove out from before us all the peoples, even the Amorites who lived in the land. Therefore we also will serve Yahweh; for he is our God.”
Joshua said to the people, “You can’t serve Yahweh, for he is a holy God. He is a jealous God. He will not forgive your disobedience nor your sins.
If you forsake Yahweh, and serve foreign gods, then he will turn and do you evil, and consume you, after he has done you good.”
The people said to Joshua, “No, but we will serve Yahweh.”
Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen Yahweh yourselves, to serve him.” They said, “We are witnesses.”
“Now therefore put away the foreign gods which are among you, and incline your heart to Yahweh, the God of Israel.”
The people said to Joshua, “We will serve Yahweh our God, and we will listen to his voice.”
So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and made for them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem.
Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God; and he took a great stone, and set it up there under the oak that was by the sanctuary of Yahweh.

Joshua said to all the people, “Behold, this stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all Yahweh’s words which he spoke to us. It shall be therefore a witness against you, lest you deny your God.”
So Joshua sent the people away, each to his own inheritance.
After these things, Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Yahweh, died, being one hundred ten years old.
They buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnathserah, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, on the north of the mountain of Gaash.
Israel served Yahweh all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, and had known all the work of Yahweh, that he had worked for Israel.

They buried the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of silver.  They became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.
Eleazar the son of Aaron died. They buried him in the hill of Phinehas his son, which was given him in the hill country of Ephraim.

footnotes.content: Shechem—the place where Abraham first pitched his tent, where Jacob built an altar—now holds the assembled people. Joshua calls the whole nation to stand before the Lord together, not scattered. When God gathers His people to hear His word, we're meant to hear it as one body.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua begins by reminding them: your grandfathers served other gods. He doesn't hide the past—he holds it up so they see how far grace has brought them. The Lord speaks plainly about what was, so we can choose freely what comes next.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham had to leave everything he knew—his country, his father's house—with only God's promise to hold onto. The Lord shows them this was never about the size of Abraham's family or his wealth at first; it was about trust. That same God asks the same trust of us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Esau got Mount Seir; Jacob's line went to Egypt—the Lord didn't lose track of either. He keeps His covenant even when a son chooses another path. And He brought Jacob's children home again. The Lord's faithfulness isn't measured by straight lines; He's faithful through the whole story.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses and Aaron—the Lord sent real leaders, real men, to stand for His people. And the plagues were real too, not metaphor. The Lord doesn't save us in a dream; He comes into the hard earth and does hard work to free His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Red Sea—that water became a wall and a tomb. It marks the place where the Lord said 'No more slavery.' Every time Israel saw the sea after that, they knew: He keeps His promise to break every chain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord put darkness between His people and their enemies—a shield of shadow so they could see the deliverance but the pursuers were blinded. Your eyes saw what the Lord did. He saved them so they'd know, so they'd remember, so they'd tell their children.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Amorites came at them with armies; the Lord gave them into your hand. Not because Israel was stronger, but because the Lord's word came before them like a consuming fire. When the Lord fights for us, the victory is already won.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Balak rose against Israel and hired Balaam to curse them—a king who saw the people and their God and thought, 'I need a curse to stop them.' Fear makes us reach for dark remedies.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord would not listen to Balaam. A curse meant for God's people turned into a blessing instead—the words came out backwards, praise where curse was meant. Not because Balaam suddenly obeyed, but because the Lord shut Balaam's mouth and opened his blessing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jericho—the name means 'the moon'—held seven nations behind walls. And the Lord delivered them all into your hand. That conquest began not with a sword but with a walk around the city and a shout of faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The hornet came before them—not your sword, not your bow. The Lord often wins our battles before we lift a hand. He clears the path. We walk it. His strength is made perfect in our weakness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You live in a land you didn't build, eat from vineyards you didn't plant. This is what grace looks like—not earned, received. The Lord gives us the fruit of labors we never did, the home we never made ready. We live by gift, not by our own hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fear Yahweh, serve Him in sincerity and truth. Put away the foreign gods. Joshua stands at the edge of the land and says: now you choose, but choose real. Don't mix the Lord with the gods your fathers served; half-faithfulness is still unfaithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If it seems evil to you to serve Yahweh—Joshua speaks as if the choice is real, as if some might turn back. But then he stands in his own house, his own will, and says: as for me and my house, we will serve Yahweh. His witness is his choice, made public, made first.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The people answer immediately—Far be it from us! They were not dragged to this moment; they chose it. Joshua's faithfulness gave them room to choose the same faithfulness. A leader's courage can unlock the courage in others.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The people recount what the Lord did for them and their fathers—deliverance from Egypt, signs in the sky, provision through the desert, safety among hostile peoples. Memory is the root of faith. When we forget what the Lord has done, we forget who He is.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They make their confession together: the Lord is our God. Not 'might be,' not 'could be'—is. This is the voice of a people who have seen Him work and now claim Him as their own. Their God. This is what covenant faith sounds like.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua warns them: you can't serve Yahweh. Not because the Lord wants to discourage them, but because they need to know what they're choosing. He is holy—not like other gods. He requires truth, not just words. He is a jealous God—He will not share your heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If you forsake Yahweh and serve foreign gods, He will turn and do you evil, and consume you. Joshua doesn't sweeten this. The Lord's mercy is real, but so is His judgment. The choice to turn from Him has real weight, real consequence. Love that doesn't warn isn't love.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No, but we will serve Yahweh. The people speak again—not less convinced by the warning, but more resolved. They hear the cost and say yes anyway. This is faith, not blind hope but eyes-wide-open choice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua makes them witnesses against themselves—you have chosen Yahweh. He holds up a mirror: you did this. Not pressure, but clarity. When we choose the Lord, that choice belongs to us; we own it. We are witnesses to our own faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Put away the foreign gods which are among you. Joshua names it plainly: they still have them. Even now, after all they've seen, they cling to the old gods tucked in their tents. The call to the Lord is always also a call to let go of what we've been holding.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We will serve Yahweh our God, and we will listen to his voice. The people commit not just to Him, but to hearing Him, to obeying Him. Listening is the bridge between loving and serving—we serve the God whose voice we've learned to hear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua made a covenant with them that day—the word 'covenant' means 'cut,' binding in blood. What began as a choice became a bond, written and witnessed. At Shechem, the nation was remade.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God and set up a great stone under the oak by the sanctuary. Written words, a stone standing still—the Lord says to His people, 'I will not forget. I hold your choice forever.' Covenant is not a whisper; it's carved in stone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all Yahweh's words. Joshua speaks to the stone as if it listens, as if the very earth remembers the Lord's faithfulness. The whole creation holds us accountable to what we've promised.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua sent the people away, each to his own inheritance. The ceremony ended; now they go home—to live it out, to make the covenant real in their daily lives. The greatest words are nothing until they're lived.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Yahweh, died—one hundred ten years old. A life span of full seasons, and every one in the Lord's service. The title 'servant of Yahweh' is carved on his grave.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They buried him in Timnathserah in the hill country of Ephraim—not in a great monument, but in his own inheritance, in the land he helped his people claim. He rests in what he fought for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Israel served Yahweh all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who had known all the work of Yahweh. Readers today hear an echo: a generation that has seen the Lord's hand at work shapes the faithfulness of the generation after. We carry what we've witnessed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They buried the bones of Joseph in Shechem—the same place where Jacob's sons once betrayed him, where he was sold into slavery. Now his bones come home. What was lost is found. What was scattered is gathered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eleazar the son of Aaron died. With him dies the last of the generation that knew Egypt and the wilderness. The old guard passes. The people now depend on the words written in stone and on their own choice to remember the Lord's faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
